input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. action.description: What to do. Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). # v0.1 reconstruction: kernel brief (shared by every agent of the kernel phase)

## Context

- Repository `/Users/guygouri/Devlab/ernlang/ern`, branch `reference/memory-model-v0`. Lake project `formal/`
  (Lean 4, no Mathlib). Build from `formal/` with `~/.elan/bin/lake`.

  clause numbers are those of v0, with the new item §63.9. v0 is history: never cite it.

  `SP=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guygouri-Devlab-ernlang-ern/c986905c-e900-4fd9-bebc-4a3ce7ebb180/scratchpad/ref`.

## Hard rules (in addition to AGENTS.md)

- No `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom`, `native_decide`, `noncomputable`, `set_option`. No warnings.
- Every constant's axioms must be within {propext, Quot.sound}. `Classical.choice` is NOT allowed. Avoid
  `Classical`, `by_contra` on non-decidable props, `Decidable.byContradiction` on classical instances,
  `simp` lemmas that pull `Classical.choice` (check if unsure with `#print axioms` in a scratch file
  under `SP/`).
- Every def/theorem docstring cites the clause it formalizes (`§63.9`, `§69.2`, ...). Module headers that
  name the spec file must name `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md`.
- Everything in English. Do not commit; do not touch git state (no stash, checkout, reset).
- Never weaken a statement, never add an unjustified hypothesis, never change a definition to make a
  proof go through. If a proof is stuck on a goal you believe false, build a concrete counterexample
  (a `decide`-checked state) if you can, stop and report the goal state.
- New helper lemmas you add to a file that other agents do not own must be `private` or carry a
  file-specific prefix, so that two files never define the same public name.

## Fixed design (decided by the orchestrator; do not deviate, report instead)

D1 Pinning obligations (v0.1 §74, §75; arbitration Q23 B#45).
  - In `Basic.lean`, add
    `structure PinOb where place : Nat; leaves : List Nat; active : Bool` (deriving DecidableEq, Repr):
    a dynamic pinning obligation, its identity being its index in `S3.pins`.
  - Replace the field `S3.pin : Nat → Bool` by `pins : List PinOb`.
  - Define `S3.pin (s : S3) (l : Nat) : Bool := s.pins.any fun o => o.active && o.leaves.contains l`
    (a leaf is dynamically pinned while an active obligation covers it), so that existing uses
    `s.pin l = false` keep their meaning.
  - `pinEff s p := { s with pins := s.pins ++ [⟨p, footprint s.P p, true⟩] }` (fresh identity = index).
  - `unpin` takes an obligation identity `o`. Effect: obligation `o` becomes inactive, nothing else changes.
    `UnpinPre k s o`: obligation `o` exists and is active; its place is usable; `HasRight s .modify place`;
    `k.ExternalDone o`.
  - `K.ExternalDone : Nat → Prop` keeps its type; it now applies to obligation identities (fix docstring).
  - `enterEff`, `allocEff`, `S3.init` no longer touch pins (`S3.init`: `pins := []`).
  - `PinPre` unchanged.
D2 Grounding of a right (v0.1 §63.4, §69.2, §70.3; follow-up answer "Q3 (suite)").
  - `Grounds (s : S3) (m : Mode) (q g : Nat) : Prop :=`
    `g ∈ List.range s.A.length ∧ s.ExercisableAt g m ∧ ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P q, Allows (effective s g l) m`
    (HasRight s m q ↔ ∃ g, Grounds s m q g; prove this lemma).
  - `RightChain (s : S3) (g j : Nat) : Prop := j = g ∨ j ∈ s.ancs g` (`ancs` = strict ancestors).
  - Both decidable. Place them in `Basic.lean` (after `HasRight`) or `Ops.lean`.
D3 `TransferPre` (Ops.lean).
  - Keep `srcRight : HasRight s .modify src`.
  - `noOutsideDerived` becomes: `∃ g ∈ List.range s.A.length, Grounds s .modify src g ∧`
    `∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, ActiveDerivedOutside s src j → RightChain s g j` (v0.1 §63.4).
  - New field `dstUsableAfter : (transferEff s src dst).Usable dst` (v0.1 §63.9).
D4 `EndUsePre` (Ops.lean).
  - `access` becomes: `∃ g ∈ List.range s.A.length, Grounds s .modify p g ∧`

  - New field `keptDesc : ∀ a ∈ List.range s.A.length, ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, s.Active a →`
    `¬ (endUseEff s p).Active a → a ∈ s.ancs j → ¬ (endUseEff s p).Active j` (v0.1 §69.2, last
    sentence: an authority the step makes inactive keeps no active descendant).
D5 `FreePre` (Ops.lean): same two changes, with `FreeAccessOK` and `freeEff` (v0.1 §70.3).
D6 `AllocStatic` (Ops.lean): new field `providerUsable : s.Usable provider` (v0.1 §71.2).
D7 `DerivePre` (Ops.lean): new field `chainActive : ∀ x ∈ s.ancs src, s.Active x` (v0.1 §60.1: every
   authority of the origin chain, effective anchor included, is active; `src` itself is `active`).
D8 `I2` (Invariants.lean, v0.1 §51): add the conjunct `(y.active = true → x.active = true)` for the origin
   `x` of `y`. Keep the mode and footprint conjuncts.
D9 `I5` (Invariants.lean, v0.1 §57), quantified over the leaves of the state ("every pinned leaf"):
   `def I5 (k : K) (s : S3) : Prop := ∀ l, l < s.P.length → isLeaf s.P l → (k.Pinned l ∨ s.pin l = true) →`
   `∃ q, s.Usable q ∧ l ∈ footprint s.P q`.

   constrained `K.Pinned` on indices that are not leaves of the state, which §57 does not say.)
   It is not part of `KInv` (§57 keeps I5 a specialized obligation of `K.Pinned`). Its reachability
   theorem carries no hypothesis on `K.Pinned` beyond what the proof needs (report any).
D10 `StaticsOK` (Invariants.lean): docstring now cites v0.1 §47 (acyclic ownership of statics) and §49
   (ordering of identifiers used to represent well-foundedness). Definition unchanged.
D11 Auxiliary invariants: `KAux`, `HeldAnchored` and any new auxiliary invariant you need (for example
   "every obligation's leaves are existing leaves") are allowed only as auxiliary, documented as "not a
   clause of §57", and must be proved to hold initially and to be preserved by every step, so that the
   §57 statement on reachable states carries no extra hypothesis.
D12 Theorems expected at the end of the kernel phase (Main.lean):
   - every step preserves `KInv` from states satisfying `KInv` and the auxiliaries (DDSound for split);
     `transfer` is no longer an exception;
   - `reachable_kinv : DDSound k → StaticsOK statics → Reachable k statics s → KInv s` (no other hypothesis);
   - I5 on reachable states (D9);
   - the v0 counterexample run of §63 (ownership cycle through `transfer`, previously
     `transfer_breaks_kinv`/`reachable_kinv_false`) is rejected under v0.1 by §63.9: keep it as a
     witness theorem stating the rejection;
   - remove what v0.1 makes obsolete: `reachable_kinv_false`, `KStepDU`, `ReachableDU` and their
     theorems, `transfer_kinv_iff` (replace by plain preservation);
   - keep: step/reachable correspondence, `op_fail_only_alloc`, base frame, `init_kinv`, `init_statics`,
     `init_only_by_writes`, `init_history`, `exitFrame_no_dangling`, `call_params_effective_protected`,
     `effective_exclusive`, and every other v0 obligation theorem, re-proved.

## File ownership and build protocol

- Stage 1 (one agent): `Basic.lean`, `Ops.lean`, `Invariants.lean`, `Lemmas.lean`, `Preserve/Common.lean`

# ERN — Memory Model Specification v0.1

**Edition v0.1 — corrective candidate, not yet validated**

Modified clauses, relative to v0 (each change is justified by a defect found while formalizing v0):

- §36: `MetaRight` governs authorities over existing storage, not the fresh allocation of `alloc`; §36 and §71.2 contradicted each other.
- §40: `RootHeld` restricted to usable root places, as in §49.7; the two clauses differed on unusable root places.
- §47: the ownership graph of statics is acyclic; a static ownership cycle made §57 false in the initial state.
- §51: a valid origin is an active origin; "valid" was undefined there.
- §57: definition of I5, which v0 named without defining.
- §59: "access operations" are O9–O11; read as all operations, §59 contradicted §69.
- §60.1: a valid origin chain is an active one, read through §44.
- §63.4: the active derived authorities covering the source from outside are named, and the authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right are exempt; without this exemption no value could be moved through a derived authority.
- §63.9 (new): the destination is usable in the resulting state; without it an accepted transfer could create an ownership cycle and break §49.8 and §57.
- §69.2 and §70.3: the same exemption as §63.4, and rejection when an authority made inactive by the step keeps an active descendant; without it an accepted step left an active authority with an inactive origin.
- §71.2: the provider is a usable place; v0 did not require it to exist.
- §74 and §75: each `pin` installs an obligation of fresh identity and `unpin` ends one designated obligation; per-leaf pin flags let an `unpin` lift a pin installed by another `pin`.
- §76.6: the reading of the precondition (whole kernel state, `ArenaInv` of the new entry, resulting state); v0 admitted several readings with different verdicts.
- §78.3: restricted to anchors covering a leaf of the administered storage; as written, its second sentence was false.
- §82.2: address and provenance of a pointer to a region whose leaves all have zero physical size; v0 decided no address for that region.
- §86: the last sentence is rewritten; as written, it was false, since `reset` and `issue` leave a recycled leaf `Init` and readable.

**Higher normative authority:** *ERN — Language Charter v0* (October 27, 2026).  
This specification defines the normative rules of ERN's memory model. Technical names (`derive`, `transfer`, `issue`, etc.) designate **abstract semantic operations**; they do not constitute syntax decisions.

## 36. Shared Mutation and Internal Administration

An abstraction may keep its metadata in `SharedMutable` storage and modify it through `writeShared` to the extent permitted by the applicable rights and contracts. **Shared mutation of metadata does not, however, grant the right to create, recycle, or terminate exclusive authority over the administered storage.** Such operations require `internal` to be exercisable in `Modify` mode from the value administering the storage.

For every administrative abstraction, including arenas, `HandlePool`, and `DataStack`, **`MetaRight` requires `Modify` exercisable on the administering value**. The `writeShared` branch alone is insufficient. `MetaRight` governs the creation or recycling of authorities over existing storage; it does not govern the creation of a fresh allocation by `alloc` (Section 71). Concurrency between calls belongs to Spec 2. Operations issuing, recycling, ending, or invalidating regions must preserve active authorities and dependencies. Allocation through administration shared among simultaneous holders, under an interface not providing such exclusive exercise, cannot be expressed in safe code with only these sequential operations: any synchronized implementation of it belongs to Spec 2. These abstractions remain libraries and add no rights to the kernel.

## 37. Dependent Values and Persistent References
## 46. Arenas as Library Administration States

Each entry belongs to the library's abstract state, **separate from kernel state `S₃`**. It has the following fields:

```text
ArenaEntry {
    storage: PlaceId
    internal: AuthorityId
    available: Set<Leaf>
    issued: Set<(Region, AuthorityId)>
}
```

A region is **available if and only if each of its leaves belongs to `available`**; the empty region is always available. Issuance removes the leaves of the issued region from `available`. Reset restores all leaves of the administered storage to that set. The registry and its updates belong to the abstraction contract and create no kernel permissions.

The arena is **live** if `internal` is active. The **arena value** is the place holding `internal`, distinct from the possible owner of `storage`. Administered storage may be local, static, allocated, or issued by another arena, under `newArena` preconditions and applicable invariants. `available` and `issued` remain **in the library's arena entry**.

## 47. Initial State

The kernel's initial state contains only base frame 0 and the declared static storage. Every static leaf has its declared initial state, `Init` or `Uninit`. The roots of static places directly owned by frame 0 have a root `Modify` authority held by that frame; a static may also be owned by another static, in which case its root authority is held by the latter. The ownership graph of statics is acyclic: no static is owned, directly or transitively, by itself. The initial state invents no dynamic allocation, derived authority, or implicit anchor. The initial arena registry belongs to library state and is empty. The initial frame does not exit.

## 48. External Parametric Contract

`K` contains the predicates `DeclaredDisjoint`, `SharedMutable`, `Pinned`, `ExternalDone`, `Deallocable`, `FreeCompat`, and `Satisfiable`. Their obligations are specified in Section 80. `K` can neither fabricate access rights nor remove an obligation of the Charter. The predicate `Invalidates` is not part of this contract.

# VII. Invariants of Reachable States

Machine states are subject to structural, validity, and exclusivity requirements preserved by permitted transitions under their declared external contracts.

## 49. WF3 — Well-Formedness of Frames, Places, and Authorities

`WF3(s)` is a **predicate on state `s`**. It jointly requires:

1. a nonempty, duplicate-free frame stack, every frame having a valid identity and, except for the base frame, a valid parent; frame-parent relations are well-founded;
2. a place structure whose composition links are valid and **acyclic**; every structural part shares its parent's owner and death marker;
3. valid owners of type frame or place, and **well-founded** ownership chains reaching a live frame for every usable place;
4. footprints consisting exclusively of leaves of existing places;
5. authorities with valid identities and modes, whose existing origins form **acyclic** chains ending at a root authority;
6. `RootChain`: every origin chain of an authority covering a leaf ends at the root of the **same structural root place** as that leaf;
7. `RootHeld`: every usable root place has its active root `Modify` authority, with no origin, held exactly by its owner;
8. holder validity: every active authority is held by a frame present in the stack or by a usable place.

Numerical ordering of identifiers, parent precedence over child in a list, and bounds on generated identifiers may be used **to represent or prove** this well-formedness in a formalization; they are not normative restrictions on place or authority identities. Preservation of `WF3` by a transition is a **required property of transitions**, not an additional clause of the state predicate. `WF3` does not impose any particular physical object layout: that belongs to refinement into the elementary memory machine.

## 50. I1 — Structural Exclusivity

For two active authorities **unrelated by derivation** covering the same leaf, their own modes must both be `Observe`. This rule also applies to leaves identified as `SharedMutable`; their particular mutation is governed by the `writeShared` contract and creates no exception to I1.

Exclusivity of **effective** modes (`effective_exclusive`) is a consequence of I1 and the definition of `effective`, not the definition of I1. On a leaf, two incompatible authorities cannot simultaneously possess incompatible effective rights. The only permitted independent ordinary coexistence is `Observe` / `Observe`.

## 51. I2 — Conservation of Rights

A derived authority covers only a subfootprint of what its origin chain permits and does not elevate its mode. Derivation and splitting restrictions do not allow duplication of an exclusive right over a leaf. Every active authority is linked to a valid origin according to state and reanchoring rules: an origin is **valid** if and only if it is active, so the origin of an active derived authority is active. Partial suspension follows from `effective`.

## 52. I3 — Validity of Anchors and Dependencies

Every explicit anchor of a still-usable place is valid. An operation cannot invalidate an anchor retained by a place that remains usable. Transitive propagation of dependencies from contained values does not change this obligation. Dependencies are not permissions and are insufficient to justify an access.

## 53. I4 — Consumption and Movement

A `Moved` leaf cannot be read as if it still contained its previous value. Moving a value does not preserve two copies of an exclusive authority. Initialization state and authority-exercise state are separate checks.

## 54. Anchor Ordering and Absence of Orphan Rights

`AnchorOrder` and `AnchorOrderHeld` are defined in Section 44. `NoDangling` prohibits an **active** authority from covering a leaf belonging to an unusable place; the invariant does not say that a leaf is initialized. `NoOrphan` requires every active authority held by a place to be connected to a frame in the stack through a **finite, non-repeating chain** of authorities: the first link is held by a live frame, and each active link **structurally covers the entirety** of the place holding the next link. The link need not have an effective mode over that place. `NoOrphan` guarantees neither the exercisability of all stored authorities nor freedom from blocking.

## 55. ArenaInv — Invariant of the Arena Abstraction

`ArenaInv` is an invariant of the **library contract**, not an additional predicate of kernel state. For every live arena:

- `storage` designates an existing, usable place; the footprint of `internal` is exactly the footprint of `storage`;
- `internal` is active, with own mode `Modify`, held by the arena value;
- available leaves and issued regions belong to the administered storage;
- two still-active issuances have disjoint regions; no leaf of a still-issued region simultaneously belongs to `available`;
- every still-issued block authority is a derivative of `internal` complying with exclusivity and validity rules;
- anchor and ownership restrictions are respected.

Arena entries do not, by themselves, constitute an additional storage owner. Two live arenas may cover common leaves when their `internal` authorities are distinct and their effective rights are compatible; no **global** disjointness of arena footprints is imposed.

## 56. Uniqueness of Live Administration

**An authority identity may serve as `internal` for at most one live administrative abstraction**, whether an arena, `HandlePool`, `DataStack`, or another library administrative instance. Before registering a new abstraction, its creation operation must jointly check the absence of that identity from **all relevant registries of live administrations**. Uniqueness concerns the identity of the `internal` authority, not merely possible overlap of footprints: abstractions with distinct `internal` identities are not forbidden merely because their footprints overlap. Library contracts must make the information required for this guard available to the creation operation; checking only an abstraction's own registry is insufficient.

**This guard is not a condition for any safety property in Section 57.** The effective right (Section 43, case 3) already prohibits a second issuance over leaves covered by an active block derived from the same authority. Rather, the guard preserves the **abstraction contract**: without it, simultaneous administration of the same `internal` could cause `reject` instead of `fail`, or reissue a previously released block that the first administration still considers unavailable. It creates neither permissions nor allocations and introduces no general detection of authority cycles. Its physical representation and encapsulation of library registries remain outside the kernel.

## 57. Main Invariant

\[
Inv3 = I1 \land I2 \land I3 \land I4 \land AnchorOrder \land NoDangling
\]

On states reachable from `S3.init statics` under `DDSound(K)`, the kernel guarantees:

\[
WF3 \land Inv3 \land AnchorOrderHeld \land NoOrphan
\]

`ArenaInv` (Section 55) belongs to the library abstraction: it is not included in this main kernel invariant.

**I5:** every pinned leaf, statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (an active pinning obligation, Section 74), belongs to a usable place.

I5, associated with pinned storage, remains a **specialized obligation** of `K.Pinned`, not a clause automatically implied by sequential accesses alone. This property is required for reachable states under the declared assumptions. Its correspondence with allocations and bytes requires the refinement defined below.

## 63. O4 — Consuming Value Transfer

**Preconditions**

1. `source` and `destination` are usable, and the current frame has exercisable `Modify` over their relevant footprints.
2. Source and destination have the **same shape of ordered subtrees**. The `i`-th child of each source part corresponds to the `i`-th child of the corresponding destination part; all nodes are matched. Structural field identity is positional, not an arbitrary matching of children.
3. **All** source leaves are `Init`, and **no** destination leaf is `Init`. The source and destination footprints are disjoint.
4. No exclusive authority is duplicated; validity of derived authorities and active projections is preserved. No active derived authority held outside `source` covers a source leaf, except the authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right over `source`: the exercisable authority on which that right rests and its origin chain. Other active authorities remain subject to this check.
5. **No in-place source leaf is pinned**, either statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (`pin`). Storage merely **owned** by the source, which is not itself moved by the transfer of that value, does not prevent this transfer.
6. Dependencies of all still-usable places following the value remain valid; non-escape constraints and `AnchorOrder` are checked in the **resulting state**, including transferred anchors of owned places that remain usable.
7. All moved held authorities, including those of owned storage, satisfy `AnchorOrderHeld` in the resulting state; no authority may escape a local anchor on the grounds that its containing value was transferred.
8. **Local self-blocking prevention:** For each active authority held before the step by a part `r` of `source` whose holder becomes the corresponding part `corr(r)` of `destination`, that authority's footprint contains **no leaf** of `corr(r)` in the resulting state. Transfer is rejected if this local check fails; no global authority-acyclicity check is imposed.
9. **Destination usability:** `destination` is usable in the resulting state.

**`ok` effect:**

- every source leaf becomes `Moved` and each corresponding destination leaf becomes `Init`;
- every authority held by source part `r` acquires as its new holder the corresponding destination part `corr(r)`, not indiscriminately the destination root;
- places owned by `r` become owned by `corr(r)`; their roots follow this owner according to `RootHeld`;
- value dependencies follow the corresponding places under validity guarantees; no authority is created or duplicated;
- destination places receive the transferred values and rights without automatically moving storage not owned by a source part.

**Other outcome:** `reject`. `transfer` to a call result is subject to these same rules.

A partially initialized structure may be transferred **field by field**, but only for fields individually eligible for transfer. This does not automatically destructure a value that owns storage **at the container level**: that storage stays with the container if the container is not transferred. Conversion between structures with permuted fields must be handled separately, not as a `transfer`.

## 67. O10 — Ordinary Write

**Preconditions**

1. Targeted leaves belong to usable places, and `access` is exercisable in `Modify` mode with **effective** `Modify` right over each leaf.
2. No incompatible ordinary authority holds an incompatible effective mode over the written leaves (I1).
3. Anchors and constraints of the relevant types, storage, and abstractions remain valid.

**`ok` effect:** The logical write sets the actually written leaves to `Init` and does not modify authorities or their anchors. An unwritten leaf does not become `Init` by this effect. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 68. O11 — Write Under Shared Mutation
## 72. O6 — Entering a Frame

**Preconditions**

1. The calling frame is the current frame and is live. Each parameter passed to the callee is an active, derived authority held by the caller before the step; the caller is **not necessarily** the frame in which the authority was first derived.
2. Modes, footprints, anchoring, and parameter-passing rules permit this change of holder; introduction of locals preserves well-formedness and the validity of their roots.
3. **Origin protection on entry:** for each `Modify` parameter with direct origin `o`, `o` is exercisable in **no mode** (neither `Observe` nor `Modify`) in the **resulting state**, once the new frame's parameters and locals have been created.
4. **G4:** `AnchorOrderHeld` is checked over the complete resulting state.

**`ok` effect:** A new child frame is pushed onto the stack; active parameters **are yielded** to that frame, which becomes their sole holder; local places and their root authorities are created; valid anchors inherited from the caller are preserved. This transfer creates no additional rights. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

This clause establishes **entry protection**. It does not prove the stronger property of protection throughout the **entire** invocation following other releases or reanchorings. While a `Modify` parameter remains active, its direct origin remains subject to effective-mode restrictions. Any additional protection throughout the invocation is deferred to Spec 3.

## 73. O7 — Exiting a Frame
## 76. O17 — Creation of an Administered Arena

**Preconditions**

1. `storage` is an existing, usable place under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame. It may be local, static, allocated, or a block issued by a previous arena.
2. `internal` is explicitly named by the caller, exists, is active, has own mode `Modify`, and `ExercisableAt(s,internal,Modify)` holds.
3. `internal` is **held by a place**: that place is the arena value; `footprint(internal) = footprint(storage)`.
4. **Unified administration guard (Section 56):** no **live** administrative abstraction, whether an arena or a library instance such as a handle pool, already uses this `internal` identity. The relevant registries of library administrations are consulted before registration. Two distinct identities may cover common leaves: this is not in itself grounds for rejection.
5. All leaves of the arena value holding `internal` are already `Init`; construction does not initialize them implicitly.
6. Dependency, holder, storage, and administration relations respect, in the resulting state, `WF3`, I1, `AnchorOrder`, and `AnchorOrderHeld` over the whole kernel state, and the new entry satisfies `ArenaInv` (Section 55).

**`ok` effect:** A live entry `{storage, internal, available, issued}` is added; the initial `available` set represents the administered storage, and `issued` is initially empty. Registering the entry fabricates no place, access right, or `Init` state. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

The identity of `internal`, not the index of `storage`, is the key to preventing duplication of live administrations. No global constraint requires footprints of live arenas to be pairwise disjoint.

## 77. O18 — Issuing an Arena Block

**Static preconditions**

1. The `arena` entry exists and is live; `internal` is active. `MetaRight` requires exercisable `Modify` over the arena value holding `internal` (Section 36). Mutation of metadata through `writeShared` alone does not satisfy this condition.
2. `region` belongs to the administered storage; `destination` is a usable **leaf** holding no active authority; the destination can legally receive the block value in mode `Modify`. The fact that `destination` is already `Init` is not in itself grounds for rejection, in accordance with O8.2.
   **Local self-blocking prevention: leaf `destination` is not in `region`, including when the region is declared available.** This condition is static and is checked before an availability `fail`.
3. Applicable **static** validity and non-escape restrictions for the destination are satisfied. The `AnchorOrder` check depending on the new anchor is performed on the **simulated resulting state**, after the availability check described in point 4; it cannot turn an unavailable issuance (`fail`) into `reject`.

**Availability and exercisability checks**

4. If static conditions hold but **at least one leaf of `region` does not belong to `available`**, the operation produces **`fail` and leaves the entire state unchanged**. The empty region is always available. An unavailable region does not permit a prior static rejection to be bypassed.
5. If the region is available, the effective mode of `internal` on that region must permit `Modify`; otherwise the outcome is `reject`.
6. The simulated result must satisfy `AnchorOrderHeld` **in the resulting state**; moreover, **in that resulting state, `destination` must remain under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame**, in accordance with O8.5. Issuance into a value with a longer lifetime than a local anchor is not made valid merely by storing it in the caller.

**`ok` effect:** A block authority of fresh identity, derived from `internal` and of mode `Modify`, is issued for the region; it is held by `destination`, which receives the corresponding anchor. The leaves of the region leave `available`, and the issuance is added to `issued` with its authority. **Only leaf `destination` becomes `Init`**; no other leaf of the arena value changes initialization. Previous issuances remain intact and valid. Issuance does not automatically install anchors on third-party values: they must use their lawful dependency mechanisms.

**Outcomes:** `ok`, `fail` (region unavailable after static validation), `reject` (static rule, effective right, or anchoring not satisfied). The destination may be a leaf of the arena value itself: its initialization then constitutes **an explicit write to that destination**, not implicit initialization of the entire arena value's metadata.

## 78. O19 — Collective Arena Reset

**Preconditions**

1. The entry exists and is live. **`MetaRight(s,arena)` requires exercisable `Modify` over the arena value**, in accordance with Section 36. `writeShared` over metadata alone, even when legal, does not replace such exercise. `internal` and the arena's other restrictions remain valid.
2. **No active authority derived from `internal` covers a leaf of the administered storage.** A derived authority with an empty footprint does not, by itself, block `reset`.
3. No still-usable place depends, directly or transitively, on an anchor in the **strict origin subtree of `internal`** (`internal` itself is excluded) that covers a leaf of the administered storage. Under precondition 2 and invariant I3, this condition follows from the absence of active descendants covering the storage, and remains explicit in the abstraction contract. Validity obligations of other nested arenas remain satisfied.

**`ok` effect:** All **leaves** of the administered storage become available again, and the issuance list is cleared under the arena contract. No still-active derived authority covering those leaves may remain, by precondition 2; an empty-footprint derivative may remain active without designating any recycled leaf. **No leaf is made `Init` by `reset`**, including in the arena value. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

Safe reuse after `reset` requires that previous issuances **covering recycled leaves**, and the dependencies on which their validity rests, have effectively ceased preventing their reuse. Any active empty-footprint derivatives cover none of those leaves. A historically issued region does not remain permanently unavailable solely for that reason.

## 86. Arena, Active Views, and Reset

Two disjoint issued regions may be used simultaneously with valid derived rights. `reset` is rejected while an issuance or active dependency would make recycling unsafe; after a legal end of use for all the relevant blocks, the region may be reissued. Reissuance modifies neither the bytes nor the initialization state. A read remains subject to the ordinary conditions of the memory model, notably `Init`, access rights, and representation validity for the requested type. Spec 4 will determine the construction and typing obligations of reissued values.

## 87. Pinning an In-Place Value

A pinned in-place leaf cannot be physically moved by `transfer`. If only an allocation owned by a value is pinned, transfer of that value may remain valid when the other conditions hold, because the owned allocation is not physically moved.

## 88. Local Self-Blocking and Indirect Cycles

An authority stored by `transfer` in a place that would then become its new holder cannot cover any leaf of that place. Likewise, `issue` cannot issue into a leaf belonging to the issued region, **or into a destination that would no longer be exercisable in `Modify` in the resulting state** (O8.5). These restrictions do not promise general freedom from authority cycles: indirect blocking compatible with safety may remain.

## 89. Handles and Persistent References

In a generation-based pool library abstraction, a handle may contain a logical pool identity, an entry identifier, and a generation. This handle is not, by itself, an access right. Safe resolution temporarily supplies authority when the pool and entry are valid; a stale identity or generation leads to defined failure. These conditions belong to the safe abstraction's contract and do not modify the authority-discipline kernel.

## 90. Global and Called Frame

# Readings — datastack (DS-v1, non-normative; spec v0 §36, §38, §46, §47, §56, §58, Part XIV, §82)

Module: `formal/Ern/Lib/DataStack.lean` (namespace `Ern.Lib.DataStack`).
Machine-checked examples: section `Witness` of that module (`run_ok`, `reading_above`,
`reading_order`, `reading_mark`, `reading_grow_dst`, `reading_newStack`, `reading_rewind_right`,
all by `decide` on library-reachable states under `Access.Examples.K0`). Four scratch files outside
the repository, re-elaborated against `b4a5cd3`: `../final5/nostack.lean` (DS-R3),
`../final5/d17.lean` and `../../records-chk/q28split.lean` (DS-R13), `../../records-chk/okonly.lean`
(R3).

Source of the contract: the brief's obligation 6 (DS-v1). Spec v0 does not define it (Part XIV
preamble: "The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and
are not defined here"). Every entry: clause, reading used, alternative, example whose verdict
changes. "[draft]" = the reading of the draft (`formal/derivability_0.1`, `Lib/DataStack.lean`),
used per policy ("use the draft's reading if the draft matches one of the readings").

## Readings that change verdicts

**DS-R1 "a cell above m" [draft].** DS-v1: "rejects if an active authority derived from internal
covers a cell above m". Reading: the cells at positions `[m.top, top)` (`above`), those that
`rewind m` returns. Alternative A: any cell at position `≥ m.top`. Alternative B: the regions issued
after `m`. Example (`Witness.reading_above`, decided): after `rewind ⟨0,1,1⟩` (top 1) and the
program's `release(5)`, `derive(4, [3], Modify)` gives authority 8, active, derived from `internal`
4, on cell 3 (position 1 ≥ `m0.top` = 0, but ≥ current top). `rewind ⟨0,0,0⟩` is `ok` here; under
A it is rejected. Safety is unaffected: the next `push` over cell 3 is rejected by the effective
right (§43, §61.1). Under B, a block grown after `m` from a base below `m` blocks `rewind` on its
lower part too (draft `opsE4`; not re-run here).

**DS-R2 order of the dead/foreign-mark `fail` and of the right of §36 [draft].** §58: "static
preconditions are checked before dynamic availability, according to the operation's contract";
DS-v1 lists "fails on a dead or foreign mark" first and says nothing about §36. Reading: mark
liveness first (`fail`), then `AdminRight` (`reject`). Alternative: §36 first. Example
(`Witness.reading_order` (1)): a callee frame with no right on the stack value rewinds to the
removed mark `⟨0,1,1⟩`: `fail` here, `reject` under the alternative. Consequence: `mark_no_aba`
gives `fail` unconditionally.

**DS-R3 "foreign" mark.** Reading: a mark is live for stack `j` iff `m.stack = j ∧ m ∈ st.marks`
(`LiveMark`); the stack identity is checked explicitly although, under `MarksWF` (proved on every
library-reachable state), membership alone implies it. The explicit identity check changes no verdict
on reachable states.
`rewind` on a stack index that does not exist is `reject` (no stack value) [draft]. This is a reason
to reject that DS-v1 does not list (narrow check ds4-2). Alternative: a mark of a stack that does not
exist is not live, so DS-v1's "fails on a dead or foreign mark" gives `fail`; or DS-v1 is silent.
Example (`../final5/nostack.lean`): on the initial state `d0` (`DReach.init`, no stack),
`rewind(0, ⟨0,0,0⟩)` is `reject` through `RewindStep.noStack` and neither `ok` nor `fail`; `fail` under
the alternative.

**DS-R4 `grow` with `extra = 0` [draft].** DS-v1 says nothing. Reading: `reject` ("grow" means a
larger size). Alternative: an in-place re-issue of the same region. Example
(`Witness.reading_order` (2)): `grow(0, 5, 0)` in `d9` is `reject`, while release, static checks,
in-place check, `split` and `store` of the same region are all `ok` (alternative: `ok`).

**DS-R5 `grow` of a live block that cannot extend in place: `fail`** (libs.md C10; DS-v1 "fail
otherwise"). The draft rejected it. Reading: the in-place check (`InPlace`: the block ends at the top
and `extra` cells follow) is the availability check of the derived issue (§77.4) and gives `fail`.
Example (`Witness.run_ok`): `grow(0, 5, 1)` in `d7`, where block 6 lies above block 5, is `fail`.
A `b` that is no block of the stack (`Stack.block` gives none): DS-v1 says nothing. Reading [draft
`case_grow`]: `reject` (`GrowStep.noBlock`). Alternative: `fail`, by analogy with DS-v1 "rewind m
fails on a dead or foreign mark" (an identifier the stack does not record). Example
(`Ern.Corpus.DataStack.DS03`, conjunct `GrowStep K0 0 6 1 ds03 .reject`, decided): after
`grow(0, 6, 1)` replaced block 6 by block 9 (`ds03.stacks` records the blocks `[⟨0, 3, 9, 5⟩]`
only), `grow(0, 6, 1)` is `reject` here and `fail` under the alternative (the step reaches
`noBlock` and no other rule).

**DS-R6 order inside `grow`.** The derived issue's static checks (`IssueStatic`) cannot be read on
the state before the release of `b` (the destination still holds `b`, §77.2 "holding no active
authority"). Reading: block lookup and `0 < extra` (`reject`); `release(b)` (`reject` if refused);
`IssueStatic` on the released state (`reject`); `InPlace` (`fail`, the state unchanged); `split`;
`store`. Alternative: in-place `fail` before the release. Changes the verdict when `b` cannot be
released and the block is not in place (`reject` here, `fail` under the alternative).

**DS-R7 `push` without room: `fail` [draft].** DS-v1 says only that `push` uses the derived issue.
Reading: the `size` cells at the top must exist (`top + size ≤ |cells|`); otherwise `fail`
(availability, §77.4), checked after `IssueStatic` on the requested cells that exist. Alternative:
"region belongs to the administered storage" (§77.2, static) gives `reject`. Example
(`Witness.reading_order` (3)): `push(0, 3, 4)` on a stack of 2 cells is `fail`.

**DS-R8 `push` static checks are those of the derived issue (`Arena.IssueStatic`, §77.1, §77.2).**
Not the draft's restricted ones: an `Init` destination is not rejected (spec v0 §77.2, O8.2).
`push` of size 0 is accepted (issue of the empty region): the empty block blocks no `rewind`, and
`rewind` forgets it in the metadata while its authority stays active [draft DS-3].

**DS-R9 `newStack` preconditions: §76.5 applies [draft]** (was R5; review round 2, DS-1). DS-v1
says nothing about creation. Reading: those of `newArena` other than its guard
(`Arena.NewArenaBase`: §76.1–§76.3 and §76.5 "All leaves of the arena value holding `internal` are
already `Init`", read for a stack) and `Guard56 (stackInternals :: others)` (§56). Alternative: drop
§76.5 for a stack (DS-v1 does not take over `newArena`). Same choice as H-R8 for pools. Example
(`Witness.reading_newStack`, decided on the initial state of statics `wsu`): leaf 0, `Uninit`, owns
the storage leaf 1 and so holds its root authority 1 (§47); `newStack(1, 1)` is `reject` (only
§76.5 fails: every other field of `NewArenaBase` and the guard hold), `ok` under the alternative.

**DS-R10 `mark` requires no right [draft]** (was R6; review round 2, DS-1). DS-v1 says nothing about
a right for `mark`. Reading: `ok` on an existing stack, `reject` on a missing one; `mark` changes
library metadata only and creates no right (§36 ¶2, §38). Alternative: §36 ¶1, metadata is modified
"to the extent permitted by the applicable rights and contracts", so `mark` needs a right on the
stack value (`AdminRight`, or a valid `writeShared` over it, §68), else `reject`. Example
(`Witness.reading_mark`): in `d13` (a callee frame entered after the rewind), the callee has no
`AdminRight`, no `Observe` right on the stack value 0 and no valid `writeShared` over it through any
authority; `mark(0)` is `ok` (a mark appended), `reject` under the alternative.

**DS-R11 `grow` destination: the recorded `Blk.dst` [draft]** (was R7; review round 2, DS-1). DS-v1
says only "grow is in place only" and "uses the derived issue"; it does not name the destination.
Reading: the destination recorded for the block at `push` (`Blk.dst`), even when the block value has
been transferred since and that place is `Moved`. Alternative: the place that currently holds `b`.
Changes the arrival state. Example (`Witness.reading_grow_dst`): after the first push (block 5
stored at place 4), the program's `transfer(4, 5)` (§63) moves authority 5 to place 5 and makes
place 4 `Moved` (`d14`). `grow(0, 5, 1)` is `ok` and stores the new block authority 6 into place 4,
which becomes `Init` (§65), while place 5 keeps the released authority 5 (`d15`). Under the
alternative, the static checks of the derived issue (`IssueStatic`) and `store(6, 5)` are `ok` on
the same released and split state, and authority 6 is held by place 5.

**DS-R12 reasons for which `rewind` rejects: §36 applies** (B47). DS-v1: "rewind m fails on a
dead or foreign mark, rejects if an active authority derived from internal covers a cell above m,
otherwise returns those cells to available and removes m and every mark above it". It names one
reason to reject. Reading: §36 applies too (normative: `MetaRight` requires `Modify` exercisable on
the stack value; the abstraction adds no rights to the kernel), so `rewind` rejects without
`AdminRight`. On library-reachable states and for an existing stack, this is the only reason outside
DS-v1's list (`rewind_ok_iff`, R3; that `ok` is then the only outcome is stated by `RewindStep.det` since `b2dcaa9`; before, it
follows from `Guarded.det`, R3). A stack index with no stack gives `reject` for another reason
outside the list, `RewindStep.noStack` (DS-R3). Alternative: DS-v1's list is exhaustive, so
`rewind` is `ok` whenever the mark is live and no such authority covers a cell above it. Example (`Witness.reading_rewind_right`,
decided): `d16` is reached by the rewind to `⟨0,1,1⟩`, the program's `release(5)` and a callee frame
with no parameter or local. There, mark `⟨0,0,0⟩` is live for stack 0 and no active authority
derived from `internal` 4 covers cell 2, the cell above it. `rewind ⟨0,0,0⟩` is `reject` here and
`ok` under the alternative. The kernel sequence cannot realize the alternative: `split` of
`internal` also rejects in `d16`, because `internal` is not exercisable at `Modify` (§61.1).
`AdminRight` has two conjuncts. `d16` tests only `MetaRight` (`internal` is active there); the other
conjunct, `internal` active, is DS-R13.

**DS-R13 a live mark of a dead stack** (narrow check ds4-3). DS-v1: "the stack keeps the ordered list
of live marks; rewind m fails on a dead or foreign mark". It does not speak of a dead stack. §46:
"The arena is **live** if `internal` is active", read for a stack by `AdminRight`. Reading:
`reject` (`RewindStep.static`), forced by the §61.1 check of the derived reset; also by the
`Active internal` conjunct of `AdminRight`. Alternative 1: DS-v1's list is exhaustive (the DS-R12
alternative): `ok`. Alternative 2: a mark of a dead stack is a dead mark: `fail` (under the DS-R2 order the mark is
checked first). Example (`../final5/d17.lean`: `d17_facts`, `d17_only_reject`): `d17` is `d11` (the
rewind to `⟨0,1,1⟩` and the program's `release(5)`) followed by the program's `release(4)` of
`internal` 4. Mark `⟨0,0,0⟩` is live for stack 0, no active authority derived from `internal` covers
cell 2, `MetaRight` still holds and `internal` is inactive. `rewind ⟨0,0,0⟩` is `reject` and nothing
else here, `ok` under alternative 1 and `fail` under alternative 2. The kernel sequence cannot
realize alternative 1: in `d17`, `split` of `internal` rejects because `internal` is inactive (§61.1;
`SplitPre.active`, the same test as the first conjunct of `AdminRight`). Without that conjunct the
outcome stays `reject` through `RewindStep.split` (`../../records-chk/q28split.lean`,
`d17_split_rejects`). So whether the liveness of the stack is part of the §36 check does not change
the verdict. The only alternatives that change it are alternative 2 (`fail`) and alternative 1
(`ok`), and alternative 1 is possible only if `rewind` skips the derived reset.

1	import Ern.MemoryModel.Arena
2	
3	/-!
4	# Handle pool: a library instance of the access discipline (non-normative)
5	
6	**Non-normative.** This module formalizes the library contract "HandlePool v0.5": the HandlePool
7	v0.4 annex (items D.1–D.4) as amended by the arbitrations Q3, Q4, Q5 and Q12 (items HP5-1 to
8	HP5-7). `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md` does not define it (Part XIV preamble: "The
9	contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and are not defined
10	here"). The normative clauses that constrain it are §36 (`MetaRight` is exercisable `Modify` on the
11	administering value; `writeShared` alone is insufficient; the library adds no rights to the
12	kernel), §37 and §89 (handles are data, not authorities; a stale identity or generation leads to
13	defined failure), §38 and §46 (library state outside `S₃`), §47 (empty initial registry), §56 (the
14	guard over all registries of live administrations), §58 (outcomes) and §76 (the obligations of
15	`newArena` that `newPool` takes over).
16	
17	The pool registry lives beside the kernel state (`PState`). Its operations are built on the
18	kernel operations O1–O16 (§60–§75): `newPool` registers only; `allocSlot` writes the handle into
19	its destination (O10); `resolve` derives a companion from `internal` over the whole storage, then
20	an entry authority from the companion (O1 twice); `resolveMany` does the same with `split` (O2) in
21	`Modify` and with one `Observe` derive per handle (O1) in `Observe`; `unresolve` releases (O3);
22	`freeSlot` updates the registry only (HP5-1). Every library step is thus, on the kernel side, a
23	finite sequence of accepted kernel steps (`pstep_kernel`), so, under `DDSound` (§80) and
24	`StaticsOK` (§47), every kernel state of a library run is kernel-reachable and satisfies the
25	invariant of §57 (`kernel_guarantee`, HP5-7).
26	-/
27	
28	namespace Ern.Lib.HandlePool
29	
30	open Ern.MemoryModel
31	open Ern.MemoryModel.Access
32	
33	/-! ## Library state (HandlePool v0.5, D.1; §38, §46) -/
34	
35	/-- Slot of a pool entry (HandlePool v0.5, D.1: `{place, gen : Nat, live : Bool}`; non-normative
36	library contract; §38, §46). -/
37	structure Slot where
38	  place : Nat
39	  gen : Nat
40	  live : Bool
41	deriving DecidableEq, Repr
42	
43	/-- Pool entry `{storage, internal, slots}` with its logical identity (HandlePool v0.5, D.1;
44	non-normative library contract). The pool value is the place holding `internal` (§46 analogue). -/
45	structure Pool where
46	  id : Nat
47	  storage : Nat
48	  internal : Nat
49	  slots : List Slot
50	deriving DecidableEq, Repr
51	
52	/-- Handle `(poolId, slot, gen)`: data, not an authority (HandlePool v0.5, D.1; §37, §89;
53	non-normative library contract). -/
54	structure Handle where
55	  id : Nat
56	  slot : Nat
57	  gen : Nat
58	deriving DecidableEq, Repr
59	
60	/-- Ghost record of a resolution (HandlePool v0.5, D.2; auxiliary information creating no right,
61	§38): pool identity and `internal`, the companion, the mode, and the entry authorities tagged with
62	their slot and resolved generation. Read by `unresolve`, by the content condition of `freeSlot`
63	(the companions of a pool, HP5-1) and by the invariants. -/
64	structure Res where
65	  pool : Nat
66	  internal : Nat
67	  comp : Nat
68	  mode : Mode
69	  entries : List (Nat × Nat × Nat)
70	deriving DecidableEq, Repr
71	
72	/-- Library state (§38, §46; HandlePool v0.5, D.1; non-normative library contract): the kernel
73	state `S₃` and, separately, the pool registry, the next fresh pool identity and the ghost
74	resolutions. -/
75	structure PState where
76	  kern : S3
77	  pools : List Pool
78	  nId : Nat
79	  res : List Res
80	
81	/-- Initial library state (§47; HandlePool v0.5, D.1): the initial kernel state, an empty
82	registry. -/
83	def PState.init (statics : Statics) : PState := ⟨S3.init statics, [], 0, []⟩
84	
85	/-- The pool read as an arena entry with nothing available or issued, to reuse `MetaRight` of §36
86	(HandlePool v0.5, D.3; non-normative library contract). -/
87	def Pool.entry (pl : Pool) : Arena.ArenaEntry := ⟨pl.storage, pl.internal, [], []⟩
88	
89	/-- Administration right on the pool (§36; HandlePool v0.5, D.3 corrected by §36, HP5-1;
90	non-normative library contract): the pool is live (`internal` active) and `MetaRight` holds,
91	exercisable `Modify` over the pool value; no `writeShared` branch. -/
92	def AdminRight (s : S3) (pl : Pool) : Prop := s.Active pl.internal ∧ Arena.MetaRight s pl.entry
93	
94	/-- Decidability of `AdminRight` (§36; HandlePool v0.5, D.3). -/
95	instance (s : S3) (pl : Pool) : Decidable (AdminRight s pl) := by
96	  unfold AdminRight; infer_instance
97	
98	/-- Place of slot `i`, `0` if absent (HandlePool v0.5, D.1; non-normative library contract;
99	§46). -/
100	def slotPlace (pl : Pool) (i : Nat) : Nat := ((pl.slots[i]?).map (·.place)).getD 0
101	
102	/-- The pool with slot `i` replaced (HandlePool v0.5, D.3; non-normative library contract;
103	§46). -/
104	def setSlot (pl : Pool) (i : Nat) (sl : Slot) : Pool := { pl with slots := pl.slots.set i sl }
105	
106	/-! ## `newPool` (HandlePool v0.5, D.1; §56, §76) -/
107	
108	/-- The pool registry as a registry of live administrations (§56; HandlePool v0.5, D.1;
109	non-normative library contract): the `internal` identities of its live pools. -/
110	def liveInternals (s : S3) (pools : List Pool) : List Nat :=
111	  (pools.filter fun pl => decide (s.Active pl.internal)).map (·.internal)
112	
113	/-- Preconditions of `newPool(storage, internal)` (HandlePool v0.5, D.1; non-normative library
114	contract; §56, §76). -/
115	structure NewPoolPre (s : S3) (pools : List Pool) (others : List (List Nat))
116	    (storage internal : Nat) : Prop where
117	  /-- HandlePool v0.5, D.1: "reprend les autres obligations applicables de `newArena`"
118	  (§76.1–§76.3, §76.5, §76.6, read on the resulting state as v0.1 §76.6 states it). -/
119	  base : Arena.NewArenaBase s storage internal
120	  /-- HandlePool v0.5, D.1: every leaf of the input storage is `Uninit`. -/
121	  uninit : ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P storage, s.I l = .uninit
122	  /-- HandlePool v0.5, D.1, §56: `internal` is absent from the pool registry and from every other
123	  registry of live administrations `others`. -/
124	  guard : Arena.Guard56 (liveInternals s pools :: others) internal
125	
126	/-- Decidability of `NewPoolPre` (HandlePool v0.5, D.1; §56, §76). -/
127	instance (s : S3) (pools : List Pool) (others : List (List Nat)) (storage internal : Nat) :
128	    Decidable (NewPoolPre s pools others storage internal) :=
129	  decidable_of_iff (Arena.NewArenaBase s storage internal ∧
130	    (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P storage, s.I l = .uninit) ∧
131	    Arena.Guard56 (liveInternals s pools :: others) internal)
132	    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c⟩ => ⟨a, b, c⟩, fun ⟨a, b, c⟩ => ⟨a, b, c⟩⟩
133	
134	/-- Effect of `newPool` (HandlePool v0.5, D.1; non-normative library contract): a pool with the
135	fresh identity `nId`, one free slot of generation zero per child of the storage, the kernel state
136	unchanged (§46, §76). -/
137	def newPoolEff (L : PState) (storage internal : Nat) : PState :=
138	  { L with
139	    pools := L.pools ++ [⟨L.nId, storage, internal,
140	      (kids L.kern.P storage).map fun q => ⟨q, 0, false⟩⟩]
141	    nId := L.nId + 1 }
142	
143	/-- `newPool` as a relation (HandlePool v0.5, D.1; §58; non-normative library contract): `ok` or
144	`reject`; `others` are the other registries of live administrations (§56). -/
145	def NewPoolStep (others : List (List Nat)) (storage internal : Nat) (L : PState) :
146	    Outcome3 PState → Prop :=
147	  Guarded (NewPoolPre L.kern L.pools others storage internal) (newPoolEff L storage internal)
148	
149	/-! ## `allocSlot` (HandlePool v0.5, D.3) -/
150	
151	/-- Static preconditions of `allocSlot(pool, dst)` (HandlePool v0.5, D.3 corrected by §36;
152	non-normative library contract). "Apte à recevoir la représentation d'un handle" names no state
153	component and is not represented. -/
154	structure AllocSlotStatic (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (dst : Nat) : Prop where
155	  /-- HandlePool v0.5, D.3, §36: live pool and `MetaRight`. -/
156	  right : AdminRight s pl
157	  /-- HandlePool v0.5, D.3: `dst` is usable. -/
158	  dstUsable : s.Usable dst
159	  /-- HandlePool v0.5, D.3: `dst` is a leaf (the handle is written into "la seule feuille
160	  `dst`"). -/
161	  dstLeaf : isLeaf s.P dst
162	  /-- HandlePool v0.5, D.3 with §67.1: the write of the handle needs exercisable `Modify` over
163	  `dst`. -/
164	  dstRight : HasRight s .modify dst
165	  /-- HandlePool v0.5, D.3: `dst` is not `Init`. -/
166	  dstNotInit : s.I dst ≠ .init
167	  /-- HandlePool v0.5, D.3: `dst` holds no active authority. -/
168	  dstFree : ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length,
169	    OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun z => z.active = true → z.holder ≠ .place dst) True
170	
171	/-- Decidability of `AllocSlotStatic` (HandlePool v0.5, D.3; §36, §67). -/
172	instance (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (dst : Nat) : Decidable (AllocSlotStatic s pl dst) :=
173	  decidable_of_iff (AdminRight s pl ∧ s.Usable dst ∧ isLeaf s.P dst ∧ HasRight s .modify dst ∧
174	    s.I dst ≠ .init ∧ ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length,
175	      OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun z => z.active = true → z.holder ≠ .place dst) True)
176	    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f⟩, fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f⟩⟩
177	
178	/-- Effect of `allocSlot` on slot `i` of pool `j` (HandlePool v0.5, D.3; non-normative library
179	contract): the slot becomes live with its generation kept; the handle is written into the leaf
180	`dst`, which alone becomes `Init` (§67 effect). -/
181	def allocSlotEff (L : PState) (j : Nat) (pl : Pool) (i : Nat) (sl : Slot) (dst : Nat) : PState :=
182	  { L with
183	    kern := write3Eff L.kern [dst]
184	    pools := L.pools.set j (setSlot pl i { sl with live := true }) }
185	
186	/-- The handle written by `allocSlot` for slot `i` (HandlePool v0.5, D.3; non-normative library
187	contract; §37, §89). -/
188	def slotHandle (pl : Pool) (i : Nat) : Option Handle :=
189	  (pl.slots[i]?).map fun sl => ⟨pl.id, i, sl.gen⟩
190	
191	/-- `allocSlot(pool j, dst)` as a relation (HandlePool v0.5, D.3; §58; non-normative library
192	contract): `reject` without the pool or a static precondition; then `fail` when no slot is free;
193	`ok` on any free slot. -/
194	inductive AllocSlotStep (j dst : Nat) (L : PState) : Outcome3 PState → Prop where
195	  | noPool : L.pools[j]? = none → AllocSlotStep j dst L .reject
196	  | static {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ¬ AllocSlotStatic L.kern pl dst →
197	      AllocSlotStep j dst L .reject
198	  | fail {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → AllocSlotStatic L.kern pl dst →
199	      (∀ sl ∈ pl.slots, sl.live = true) → AllocSlotStep j dst L .fail
200	  | ok {pl : Pool} {i : Nat} {sl : Slot} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → AllocSlotStatic L.kern pl dst →
201	      pl.slots[i]? = some sl → sl.live = false →
202	      AllocSlotStep j dst L (.ok (allocSlotEff L j pl i sl dst))
203	
204	/-! ## `resolve`, `resolveMany` (HandlePool v0.5, D.2, HP5-5, HP5-6) -/
205	
206	/-- Validity of a handle for pool `pl` (HandlePool v0.5, D.2, D.3, HP5-5, HP5-6; §89;
207	non-normative library contract): the pool is live (`internal` active, §46 analogue: a handle of a
208	dead pool is stale, HP5-5), the handle names the pool, and it designates a live slot at its
209	generation (a handle of a free entry is stale, HP5-6); a slot index outside the pool designates
210	nothing. -/
211	def HandleOK (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (h : Handle) : Prop :=
212	  s.Active pl.internal ∧ h.id = pl.id ∧
213	    OptP (pl.slots[h.slot]?) (fun sl => sl.gen = h.gen ∧ sl.live = true) False
214	
215	/-- Decidability of `HandleOK` (HandlePool v0.5, D.2; §89). -/
216	instance (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (h : Handle) : Decidable (HandleOK s pl h) := by
217	  unfold HandleOK; infer_instance
218	
219	/-- Legal exercise of `internal` at mode `m` for the companion (HandlePool v0.5, D.2;
220	non-normative library contract): the preconditions of the `derive` of the companion from
221	`internal` over all leaves of the storage (§60). -/
222	def ResolveRight (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (m : Mode) : Prop :=
223	  DerivePre s pl.internal (footprint s.P pl.storage) m
224	
225	/-- Decidability of `ResolveRight` (HandlePool v0.5, D.2; §60). -/
226	instance (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (m : Mode) : Decidable (ResolveRight s pl m) := by
227	  unfold ResolveRight; infer_instance
228	
229	/-- State after the companion (HandlePool v0.5, D.2; §60 effect; non-normative library contract):
230	authority `|A|`, derived from `internal` at mode `m` over all leaves of the storage. -/
231	def compS (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (m : Mode) : S3 :=
232	  deriveEff s pl.internal (footprint s.P pl.storage) m
233	
234	/-- Observe derivations from `c`, one per region in order (HandlePool v0.5, D.2: `resolveMany` in
235	`Observe`; §60; non-normative library contract): each accepted in the state left by the previous
236	ones. -/
237	def DerivesPre (s : S3) (c : Nat) : List (List Nat) → Prop
238	  | [] => True
239	  | r :: rs => DerivePre s c r .observe ∧ DerivesPre (deriveEff s c r .observe) c rs
240	
241	/-- Decidability of `DerivesPre` (HandlePool v0.5, D.2, §60). -/
242	instance decDerivesPre (s : S3) (c : Nat) :
243	    (rs : List (List Nat)) → Decidable (DerivesPre s c rs)
244	  | [] => isTrue trivial
245	  | r :: rs =>
246	    have := decDerivesPre (deriveEff s c r .observe) c rs
247	    inferInstanceAs (Decidable (_ ∧ _))
248	
249	/-- Effect of the `Observe` derivations from `c`, in order (HandlePool v0.5, D.2; §60 effect). -/
250	def derivesEff (s : S3) (c : Nat) : List (List Nat) → S3
251	  | [] => s
252	  | r :: rs => derivesEff (deriveEff s c r .observe) c rs
253	
254	/-- Entry authorities of a batch from the companion `c` (HandlePool v0.5, D.2; non-normative
255	library contract): `split` (§61) in `Modify`, successive `Observe` derivations (§60) in
256	`Observe`. -/
257	def EntriesPre (k : K) : Mode → S3 → Nat → List (List Nat) → Prop
258	  | .modify, s, c, rs => SplitPre k s c rs
259	  | .observe, s, c, rs => DerivesPre s c rs
260	
261	/-- Decidability of `EntriesPre` (HandlePool v0.5, D.2; §60, §61). -/
262	instance (k : K) [∀ r r', Decidable (k.DeclaredDisjoint r r')] (m : Mode) (s : S3) (c : Nat)
263	    (rs : List (List Nat)) : Decidable (EntriesPre k m s c rs) := by
264	  cases m <;> unfold EntriesPre <;> infer_instance
265	
266	/-- Effect of the entry authorities of a batch (HandlePool v0.5, D.2; §60, §61 effects). -/
267	def entriesEff : Mode → S3 → Nat → List (List Nat) → S3
268	  | .modify, s, c, rs => splitEff s c rs
269	  | .observe, s, c, rs => derivesEff s c rs
270	
271	/-- Regions of the entries designated by a batch: the footprint of each slot (HandlePool v0.5,
272	D.2; non-normative library contract; §60). -/
273	def entryRegions (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (hs : List Handle) : List (List Nat) :=
274	  hs.map fun h => footprint s.P (slotPlace pl h.slot)
275	
276	/-- Ghost entries of a batch: the `n`-th entry authority is `c + 1 + n`, for slot and generation of
277	the `n`-th handle (HandlePool v0.5, D.2; auxiliary, §38). -/
278	def batchEntries (c : Nat) (hs : List Handle) : List (Nat × Nat × Nat) :=
279	  mapI (fun i h => (i, h.slot, h.gen)) (c + 1) hs
280	
281	/-- `resolve(h, m)` on pool `j` as a relation (HandlePool v0.5, D.2, HP5-5, HP5-6; §58, §89;
282	non-normative library contract): `reject` without the pool; then `fail` for a handle of a dead
283	pool, of another pool, stale, absent or free, before the right is checked (HP5-5); then `reject`
284	without the legal exercise of `internal`; then the companion and the entry authority derived from
285	it, `reject` when the second derivation is not accepted. -/
286	inductive ResolveStep (j : Nat) (h : Handle) (m : Mode) (L : PState) : Outcome3 PState → Prop where
287	  | noPool : L.pools[j]? = none → ResolveStep j h m L .reject
288	  | fail {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ¬ HandleOK L.kern pl h →
289	      ResolveStep j h m L .fail
290	  | noRight {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → HandleOK L.kern pl h →
291	      ¬ ResolveRight L.kern pl m → ResolveStep j h m L .reject
292	  | noEntry {pl : Pool} {sl : Slot} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → HandleOK L.kern pl h →
293	      ResolveRight L.kern pl m → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl →
294	      ¬ DerivePre (compS L.kern pl m) L.kern.A.length (footprint L.kern.P sl.place) m →
295	      ResolveStep j h m L .reject
296	  | ok {pl : Pool} {sl : Slot} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → HandleOK L.kern pl h →
297	      ResolveRight L.kern pl m → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl →
298	      DerivePre (compS L.kern pl m) L.kern.A.length (footprint L.kern.P sl.place) m →
299	      ResolveStep j h m L (.ok { L with
300	        kern := deriveEff (compS L.kern pl m) L.kern.A.length (footprint L.kern.P sl.place) m
301	        res := L.res ++ [⟨pl.id, pl.internal, L.kern.A.length, m,
302	          [(L.kern.A.length + 1, h.slot, h.gen)]⟩] })
303	
304	/-- Validity of a batch (HandlePool v0.5, D.2, HP5-5; non-normative library contract): every
305	handle is valid (`HandleOK`); pairwise distinct slots in `Modify` only (§58, §89). -/
306	def BatchOK (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (hs : List Handle) (m : Mode) : Prop :=
307	  (∀ h ∈ hs, HandleOK s pl h) ∧ (m = .modify → (hs.map (·.slot)).Nodup)
308	
309	/-- Decidability of `BatchOK` (HandlePool v0.5, D.2; §58, §89). -/
310	instance (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (hs : List Handle) (m : Mode) : Decidable (BatchOK s pl hs m) := by
311	  unfold BatchOK; infer_instance
312	
313	/-- `resolveMany(hs, m)` on pool `j` as a relation (HandlePool v0.5, D.2, HP5-5; §58;
314	non-normative library contract): `reject` without the pool; then an atomic `fail` for an invalid
315	batch, before the right is checked (HP5-5); then `reject` without the legal exercise of
316	`internal`; then one companion and the entry authorities (`EntriesPre`), `reject` when they are
317	not accepted. -/
318	inductive ResolveManyStep (k : K) (j : Nat) (hs : List Handle) (m : Mode) (L : PState) :
319	    Outcome3 PState → Prop where
320	  | noPool : L.pools[j]? = none → ResolveManyStep k j hs m L .reject
321	  | fail {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ¬ BatchOK L.kern pl hs m →
322	      ResolveManyStep k j hs m L .fail
323	  | noRight {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → BatchOK L.kern pl hs m →
324	      ¬ ResolveRight L.kern pl m → ResolveManyStep k j hs m L .reject
325	  | noEntries {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → BatchOK L.kern pl hs m →
326	      ResolveRight L.kern pl m →
327	      ¬ EntriesPre k m (compS L.kern pl m) L.kern.A.length (entryRegions L.kern pl hs) →
328	      ResolveManyStep k j hs m L .reject
329	  | ok {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → BatchOK L.kern pl hs m → ResolveRight L.kern pl m →
330	      EntriesPre k m (compS L.kern pl m) L.kern.A.length (entryRegions L.kern pl hs) →
331	      ResolveManyStep k j hs m L (.ok { L with
332	        kern := entriesEff m (compS L.kern pl m) L.kern.A.length (entryRegions L.kern pl hs)
333	        res := L.res ++ [⟨pl.id, pl.internal, L.kern.A.length, m,
334	          batchEntries L.kern.A.length hs⟩] })
335	
336	/-! ## `unresolve` (HandlePool v0.5, D.2) -/
337	
338	/-- Releases the authorities of a list in order (§62); `none` as soon as one release is not
339	accepted (HandlePool v0.5, D.2: "Les règles de `release` … restent applicables"). -/
340	def releaseAll : S3 → List Nat → Option S3
341	  | s, [] => some s
342	  | s, a :: l => if ReleasePre s a then releaseAll (releaseEff s a) l else none
343	
344	/-- The resolution of companion `c` (HandlePool v0.5, D.2; ghost lookup, §38). -/
345	def findRes (L : PState) (c : Nat) : Option Res := L.res.find? fun r => r.comp == c
346	
347	/-- Authorities released by `unresolve` of `r` (HandlePool v0.5, D.2; non-normative library
348	contract): the entry authorities still active, then the companion (§62). -/
349	def unresolveList (s : S3) (r : Res) : List Nat :=
350	  ((r.entries.map (·.1)).filter fun a => decide (s.Active a)) ++ [r.comp]
351	
352	/-- `unresolve(c)` as a relation (HandlePool v0.5, D.2; §58; non-normative library contract): the
353	releases of `unresolveList`; `reject` when one is not accepted or `c` is no companion. -/
354	inductive UnresolveStep (c : Nat) (L : PState) : Outcome3 PState → Prop where
355	  | none : findRes L c = none → UnresolveStep c L .reject
356	  | reject {r : Res} : findRes L c = some r → releaseAll L.kern (unresolveList L.kern r) = none →
357	      UnresolveStep c L .reject
358	  | ok {r : Res} {s' : S3} : findRes L c = some r →
359	      releaseAll L.kern (unresolveList L.kern r) = some s' →
360	      UnresolveStep c L (.ok { L with kern := s' })

362	/-! ## `freeSlot` (HandlePool v0.5, D.3 as amended by HP5-1) -/
363	
364	/-- No active strict descendant of a companion recorded for pool `pl` covers a leaf of place `q`
365	(HandlePool v0.5, HP5-1, and D.4 (3) restricted to the companions of the slot's pool, HP5-4; §42:
366	descendants along the origin chain; non-normative library contract). The companions of `pl` are
367	those of the resolutions recorded for its identity. -/
368	def NoCompDesc (L : PState) (pl : Pool) (q : Nat) : Prop :=
369	  ∀ r ∈ L.res, r.pool = pl.id → ∀ x ∈ List.range L.kern.A.length, L.kern.Active x →
370	    r.comp ∈ L.kern.ancs x → ∀ l ∈ L.kern.afp x, l ∉ footprint L.kern.P q
371	
372	/-- Decidability of `NoCompDesc` (HandlePool v0.5, HP5-1; §42). -/
373	instance (L : PState) (pl : Pool) (q : Nat) : Decidable (NoCompDesc L pl q) := by
374	  unfold NoCompDesc; infer_instance
375	
376	/-- Content conditions of `freeSlot` on slot place `q` of pool `pl` (HandlePool v0.5, HP5-1;
377	non-normative library contract). -/
378	structure FreeContentOK (L : PState) (pl : Pool) (q : Nat) : Prop where
379	  /-- HandlePool v0.5, HP5-1: no leaf of the entry is `Init`; each is `Uninit` or `Moved`
380	  (§41). -/
381	  notInit : ∀ l ∈ footprint L.kern.P q, L.kern.I l ≠ .init
382	  /-- HandlePool v0.5, HP5-1: no active authority derived from a companion of this pool (a strict
383	  descendant of a companion recorded for this pool) covers a leaf of the entry. -/
384	  noCompDesc : NoCompDesc L pl q
385	
386	/-- Decidability of `FreeContentOK` (HandlePool v0.5, HP5-1; §41, §42). -/
387	instance (L : PState) (pl : Pool) (q : Nat) : Decidable (FreeContentOK L pl q) :=
388	  decidable_of_iff ((∀ l ∈ footprint L.kern.P q, L.kern.I l ≠ .init) ∧ NoCompDesc L pl q)
389	    ⟨fun ⟨a, b⟩ => ⟨a, b⟩, fun ⟨a, b⟩ => ⟨a, b⟩⟩
390	
391	/-- Effect of `freeSlot` on slot `i` of pool `j` (HandlePool v0.5, HP5-1; non-normative library
392	contract): the slot becomes free and its generation is incremented; there is no end-of-use effect
393	and the kernel state is unchanged (§36: the library adds no rights to the kernel). -/
394	def freeSlotEff (L : PState) (j : Nat) (pl : Pool) (i : Nat) (sl : Slot) : PState :=
395	  { L with pools := L.pools.set j (setSlot pl i ⟨sl.place, sl.gen + 1, false⟩) }
396	
397	/-- `freeSlot(h)` on pool `j` as a relation (HandlePool v0.5, D.3 corrected by §36, HP5-1; §58;
398	non-normative library contract): `reject` without the pool or without the administration right
399	(live pool and `MetaRight`); then `fail` for a handle of another pool, stale, absent or free; then
400	`reject` unless the content conditions hold (`FreeContentOK`). This is the outcome order of
401	HandlePool v0.4, kept by HP5-1: the order of HP5-5 (handle before right) concerns resolution
402	(§89) only. -/
403	inductive FreeSlotStep (j : Nat) (h : Handle) (L : PState) : Outcome3 PState → Prop where
404	  | noPool : L.pools[j]? = none → FreeSlotStep j h L .reject
405	  | noRight {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ¬ AdminRight L.kern pl →
406	      FreeSlotStep j h L .reject
407	  | fail {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → AdminRight L.kern pl → ¬ HandleOK L.kern pl h →
408	      FreeSlotStep j h L .fail
409	  | noContent {pl : Pool} {sl : Slot} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → AdminRight L.kern pl →
410	      HandleOK L.kern pl h → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl → ¬ FreeContentOK L pl sl.place →
411	      FreeSlotStep j h L .reject
412	  | ok {pl : Pool} {sl : Slot} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → AdminRight L.kern pl →
413	      HandleOK L.kern pl h → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl → FreeContentOK L pl sl.place →
414	      FreeSlotStep j h L (.ok (freeSlotEff L j pl h.slot sl))
